name: MXR Phase 90 (1974 script logo)
description: MXR Phase 90, script-logo circuit (no R28 feedback resistor, no C11 Miller cap): six single LM741 op-amps on a 9 V battery. U1a unity-gain input buffer (R3 10 kΩ / C5 10 nF / R14 470 kΩ to Vref); four inverting all-pass stages U2a/U2d/U2c/U2b (10 kΩ / 10 kΩ, 47 nF into the + input, 24 kΩ to Vref in parallel with a 2N5952 JFET voltage-controlled resistor, source at Vref); PNP 2N4125 shunt-feedback mixer (R16 dry / R8 wet 150 kΩ into the base, R7 150 kΩ base-collector, R4 56 kΩ collector load, emitter at Vref) and C2 47 nF / R2 150 kΩ output network. LFO: U1b relaxation oscillator (R19 150 kΩ / R21 470 kΩ hysteresis around Vref, R24 150 kΩ + C7 10 nF into the − input) charging C10 15 µF through the 500 kΩ reverse-log Speed rheostat R36; the C10 triangle reaches the four JFET gates through R22 3.9 MΩ, summed with the 250 kΩ bias trimmer wiper through R20 1 MΩ and filtered by C4 47 nF to Vref. Vref is the 5.1 V zener D2 fed by R15 10 kΩ (ideal source here: the engine has no zener model). The R28 24 kΩ block-logo feedback resistor is not fitted (script circuit).

controls.label: Speed
controls.note: R36: 500 kΩ reverse-log (C) pot wired as a rheostat between U1b's output and C10; clockwise = less resistance = faster. Legacy 'Rate'

controls.label: Bias trim (internal)
controls.note: Rtrimmer 250 kΩ linear trimpot from Vref (5.1 V) to ground; its wiper feeds the JFET gates through R20 1 MΩ (DC gate ≈ 0.80·Vwiper + 1.04 V). Sets where the 0.15-0.33 V LFO sweep sits on the 2N5952 curves. The factory trims each matched set by ear/scope; 0.5 puts the slow-speed sweep from just above pinch-off (gate 2.95 V) to 3.28 V with the library 2N5952 (VTO −2.2 V): first notch ≈ 250 Hz → 1.4 kHz. Below ≈ 0.44 the JFETs stay cut off (static notches 56 / 356 Hz); above ≈ 0.6 the sweep is small and high

controls.label: Sync
controls.note: Tempo sync has no part in the Phase 90; stored for preset round-trip only

controls.label: Notches
controls.note: Legacy 2-8 notch-count parameter. The Phase 90 has four all-pass stages (two notches) and no switch; stored only

controls.label: Color
controls.note: No Color control on the script Phase 90 (the nearest hardware feature is the later block-logo R28 feedback resistor, not fitted to the script circuit); stored only

controls.label: LED
controls.note: The 1974 script unit has no LED; stored only

controls.label: Invert
controls.note: No invert switch in the circuit; stored only

controls.label: Rotate
controls.note: No LFO-phase control in the circuit; stored only

controls.label: Mix
controls.note: The dry/wet ratio is fixed by R16 = R8 = 150 kΩ (50/50); no control. Stored only

controls.label: Depth
controls.note: The sweep depth is fixed by R22 3.9 MΩ / R20 1 MΩ; no control. Stored only

controls.label: Freq
controls.note: No front-panel frequency control on the Phase 90. Its nearest circuit meaning is the internal bias trimmer (control bias), but legacy values below ≈ 0.44 would park the JFETs in cut-off and silence the sweep, so it is stored only

parts.label: Vref (D2 5.1 V zener)
parts.note: Ideal 5.1 V node standing in for the zener D2 fed by R15 10 kΩ and decoupled by C8 15 µF. The engine has no zener (reverse-breakdown) diode model. D1 1N914 (reverse-polarity clamp across Vref, anode to ground) is reverse biased in normal use and omitted
Zener feed resistor; with the ideal Vref source it only adds battery current
Vref decoupling (inert across the ideal source)

parts.label: Rtrimmer (FET bias)
parts.note: unverified: 250 kΩ per ElectroSmash's BOM; Morrin's script-era unit had a 200 kΩ trimmer. Linear trimmer across Vref and ground (pin order assumed: clockwise = higher gate voltage)
Gate-line filter to Vref (ElectroSmash power-supply drawing). With R20 ∥ R22 (≈ 0.8 MΩ) it is a 4.3 Hz low-pass, which is why the sweep depth falls at high Speed

parts.label: LFO (Schmitt relaxation oscillator)
parts.note: Script units: TI uA741CP / National LM741 single op-amps (ElectroSmash, Morrin)

parts.label: Speed
parts.note: Rheostat on the wiper-to-pin-3 segment: R = 500k·(1 − t(x)); with the C (reverse-log) taper R falls from 500 kΩ (slow) to the end resistance (fast). ElectroSmash labels it R36 470K; the stock part is a 500 kΩ reverse-log pot (DIYstompboxes, Aion Zenith BOM)

unverified: NOT on the schematic. Stands in for the speed pot's end (residual) resistance plus the 741's output current limit, which the engine's op-amp and pot models lack (pot end resistance is 1 Ω in the engine). Without it the LFO runs at tens of Hz at full Speed; 4.7 kΩ gives ≈ 10 Hz, the maximum reported for the pedal (Fender forum emulation: 0.15-10 Hz). Remove when the engine models pot end resistance / op-amp current limit
LFO timing capacitor (tantalum). Some 1975 units measured 10 µF (DIYstompboxes)
Sweep-depth resistor. Older schematics show 3.3 MΩ (unverified which value the earliest script units carried)

parts.label: LFO start kick
parts.note: Simulation aid, not in the pedal: the DC operating point puts the relaxation oscillator on its unstable balance (all nodes at Vref); 1 mV through 10 MΩ into the + input starts it, as power-on transients do in the hardware

parts.label: VCR 1
parts.note: Drain at the + input, source at Vref (the channel is symmetric). Factory parts were matched sets (VGS(off) spread -1.3 to -3.5 V on the datasheet); all four use the same library model here
